name: Black seed (Nigella sativa) oil
short: Trials reported no serious adverse events. A laboratory study predicts its main compound, thymoquinone, could interact with warfarin; this has not been shown in patients.
text: In a systematic review of six randomised trials in 370 people with knee osteoarthritis, topical or oral Nigella sativa was well tolerated and no serious adverse events were reported. A systematic review and meta-analysis of trials in children likewise found no statistically significant occurrence of side effects, while noting that further studies are needed to fully understand its safety in children. A laboratory (in vitro) study found that thymoquinone, the predominant bioactive compound in the oil, inhibited an enzyme step in warfarin metabolism, and its authors predicted possible interactions in people taking warfarin; this is a prediction from laboratory data, not a finding in patients.
